x: Our glorious Devonian, Ken Venton,is beginning to show us the rewards of his hard training, and I anticipate that he and Brian Johnston will be showing us their real form in the coming road relay season.

After 2½ miles Charlie was 5th, followed by Ken Miller 28th, David Jones 46th, Ranjit Bhatia 53rd, John Moore 60th, Clive Shippen 61st, and Ken Venton 82nd, with the others at regularly spaced intervals within the first half of the field.

He was backed up by Alan Black 67th, Ken Venton 75th and John Thresher 90th. After half a mile it looked as though our lads were going to repeat their Surrey performance with Ken and Alan in the first dozen, but after a further 2 miles Ken lay 23rd, with John Thresher and Ken Venton in the 80's and…
After half-mile he, Alan Black and John Thresher were in the first 20, and with Ken Venton and Eric Penny only a little way behind— a most promising start.

A blanket finish in the 880 yds placed Alan Black 3rd (2-0.6) and Ken Venton 4th (2-0.9). Our long-jump team Jim Mc Grath and Dave Ansell scooped the long jump with 21'1" and 20'8", whilst second-claim member Hollingsworth won the discus with 151'-0½" ( what a great prospect this fellow is!)
Ken Venton, now stationed at Taunton with the R.A.P.C., finished 8th in the Devon County cross country championships---one place ahead of Olympic athlete Brian Kent-Smith.
Others like David Jones, Don Maclean, Ken Venton and our newly promoted Youths will be endeavouring to reach that "top 12" also, so a few fireworks would not be amiss!

In the Civil Service cross country championships, held on Wednesday February 21st, Charlie Walker qualified for the Civil Service team for the third time by finishing 5th. Ken Venton also competed and was placed 15th.
